In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuronal nicotonic receptor is a membrane receptor which displays a low deltaCo(p), is thermodynamically discriminating and obeys the enthalpy- entropy compensation phenomenon.

the thermodynamic parameters of the binding equilibrium at the neuronal nicotinergic receptor can be considered as the sum of two terms: a) the intrinsic thermodynamic parameters of binding, which are determined by the nature of the ligand and of the receptor and which are not affected by the environment in which the receptor is embedded; b) a contribution from the receptor environment, which is mainly determined by the lipid bilayer and which is common to all membrane receptors.

the thermodynamic parameters of the ligand-receptor binding equilibrium can be used as a tool to discriminate between agonists and antagonist ligands at a receptor site, and that the phenomenon of enthalpic/entropic compensation is a recurrent phenomenon which has been observed in all membrane receptors studied so far.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermodynamic properties of ligand binding to membrane receptors are not only useful in the study of receptor-ligand interactions, but also represent a useful tool for the understanding of the mechanism of action of the receptors.

, in general, the thermodynamic properties of ligand-receptor interactions are determined by the nature of the binding sites and the conformational changes they undergo, and that, in particular, the thermodynamics of the binding of agonists to ligand-gated receptors are determined by a delicate balance between the enthalpic contribution of the binding site and the entropy contribution of the receptor conformational changes.

the binding of agonists to the nicotinic receptor is enthalpy-driven, while antagonists are entropy-driven, and that both agonistic and antagonistic binding to the receptor is accompanied by a large negative heat capacity change.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of membrane receptors, the thermodynamic discrimination between ligands of different pharmacological activity, such as agonists and antagonistic, can be achieved by the combined effect of the enthalpic and entropic contributions to ligand binding.
